title: Sitting in with the Eagle Band; uptown versus downtown players
summary: At about ten he played Bunk's cornet at the animals ball; he contrasts downtown readers like Perez with uptown players such as Oliver, Bunk and Joe Johnson.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Fiddlers and reading violinists of New Orleans

blocks.x: Yeah Foots was a great band. Foots was a great band. So Foots was with the Eagle Band and Frankie Dusen and Pache was a little boy that was playing clarinet in this band. So all the guys, when I walked in the place, Foots bought me and they thought I was Frankie Dusen's part because I looked like Frankie at that time. Frankie was slant and they were resembled each other. So they had wore uniforms, I'm going to get them, all them brown uniforms at that time. And I put on Bunk's Eagle cap and picked up his counter and started playing at the animals ball. And I knew he didn't play. How old were you about? I was about ten years old at that time. My aunt and I had moved down on Gasket Street and I was living so far from the funky but all at that time. So my daddy wanted me to be strictly by the music. So I knew practically all the old downtown musicians were musicians like Manuel Perez, they read music but they didn't have that spirit. Those uptown boys had like Joe Oliver and Bunk and all the rest of the boys, another boy they called, Johnson, was no kin to Bunk, was a good cornet player.
